dimensions.name: Interpreter & SIMD-encoding orientation

evidence.note: Read all source files fully (decode.rs 434, runtime.rs 758, spec.rs 408, types.rs 170), even copying to /tmp to overcome truncation; built an explicit map distinguishing what compiles vs which functions are stubbed/buggy (exec_numeric, Call/CallIndirect, V128 lane helpers, validate_module) and noted the V128 type already exists in types.rs and the frozen spec.rs/main.rs contract.

Installed wabt and used wasm2wat + wasm-objdump to decode SIMD test binaries, then wrote a Python script to extract all 0xFD sub-opcodes from every test WASM — verifying the exact encoding against wabt-generated output rather than guessing the opcode mapping.

Sustained, targeted re-research as unfamiliar families were reached: probed specific spec-test failures to pin down pmin/pmax NaN semantics, lane load/store operand order, sign extension (0x80→-128), -0.0 preservation in rounding, and the trap-text distinction between 'invalid conversion to integer' (NaN/inf) vs 'integer overflow' (out-of-range).

Discovered concretely that Simd/V128Const variants weren't wired and that decode relied on `use Instr::*`; corrected while respecting the frozen public items, showing orientation to the real interface constraints.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent exhaustively read the skeleton, cataloged stubbed-vs-buggy functions and the frozen public API, and empirically derived the 0xFD encoding from wabt-decoded test binaries rather than guessing — matching the level-8 anchor. It then sustained deep, per-family re-research (NaN, saturation, sign/lane order, trap text) driven by specific spec-test cases and confirmed encoding against wabt output, which is the defining behavior of the level-10 anchor. I place it at 9 rather than a perfect 10 because verification of the public API surface was handled somewhat reactively (via a build error) rather than proactively enumerated up front.

dimensions.name: Family-level decomposition & milestones

evidence.note: After exploration, agent enumerated gaps (validate_module, exec_numeric, Call/CallIndirect, SIMD decode/execute, V128 helpers) but framed them as a flat to-do list, not an ordered family-level milestone plan.
SIMD was implemented as one monolithic push — full SimdOp enum, decode_simd (236 opcodes) and exec_simd written at once — rather than a planned family-by-family sequence with staged done-checks.
Clear MVP-before-SIMD ordering: got i32/block/return to 100% via validation+call fixes before deeply engaging SIMD execution.

Family-bucket checkpointing appears reactively: simd_bitwise 167/167, simd_lane 463/463, int_to_int_extend 252/252 used as per-family done-checks — matching anchor 5's 'matching spec test as a rough checkpoint.'

Repeated flip-flopping (lane operand order, pmin/pmax, extadd_pairwise unary/binary, conversion trap types) causing regressions — the decomposition was not a clean rework-avoiding hierarchy, keeping it well below anchor 8/10.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent sequenced MVP correctness before SIMD and, during debugging, grouped SIMD into families each validated against its own spec_json file — squarely anchor 5. It falls short of 8 because there was no explicit upfront ordered plan over the ~15 families with dependency ordering and pass targets; the family structure emerged reactively from failure buckets after a single monolithic SIMD implementation, and repeated flip-flopping of fixes shows the absence of the disciplined, rework-avoiding milestone hierarchy the higher anchors require. It is above 3 because real per-family done-criteria (spec-test pass counts) were consistently used.

dimensions.name: Incremental per-family verification

evidence.note: From the start ran individual per-family jsons (i32.json, block.json, return.json, simd/simd_const.json) after building, reading per-file pass counts (376/459, 66/222, 444/445) to localize where failures lived rather than only the aggregate.

Created and repeatedly invoked the aggregate run_tests.py runner, tracking the score as a monitored signal (35.2% → 39.67% → 96.21% ...) and re-running after fixes to confirm movement, not as a one-shot final check.

Systematic per-family loop after SIMD implementation: ran simd_lane/simd_bitwise/simd_const, read specific FAIL reasons ('stack underflow', 'type error: expected v128', 'no current module'), even cross-checked with wasm-validate to distinguish decode errors from execution bugs.

Detected a regression (96.21% → 95.93% after a change), diagnosed genuine bugs vs encoding mismatches — decode_simd opcode-mapping errors vs trap-text mismatches — and semantic edge cases like NaN handling in pmin/pmax (688 failures traced to wasm_f32_min vs a.min).

Late-stage drilling into individual failing assertions: narrow-op signed/unsigned saturation boundaries (fixed → simd_conversions 100%), -0.0 sign preservation in ceil/floor, trunc_u sign semantics; noticed a trunc_u fix caused regressions and reverted; explicitly kept pursuing exact 1.0, treating 99.95% as insufficient.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent ran per-family spec-test jsons after implementing each family, read specific FAIL @ line reasons, fixed, and re-ran to green while periodically running the aggregate runner to guard MVP files against SIMD-induced regressions — comfortably beyond the level-8 anchor. It further engineered verification: drilling into individual assertions to diagnose NaN handling, saturation boundaries, sign, and lane/operand order; distinguishing genuine semantic bugs from opcode-encoding mismatches; catching and reverting a regression; and monitoring the aggregate score as a live signal while explicitly refusing to settle for 'mostly passing' below 1.0 — matching nearly all of the level-10 description. I withhold a full 10 only because of repetitive churn on the same trap-text issue and brief 'rather than fix every last test' wavering before pressing on.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the opcode surface

evidence.note: Quantifies 1098 remaining failures across 26 files and ranks them by bucket size (pmin/pmax 688, lane load/store 112, conversions 49...) to target highest-remaining families first — top-anchor reallocation behavior.

Precise per-family pass counts continuously reconciled: block/i32/return 100%, call 89/90, call_indirect 161/169, simd_lane 189/463, simd_bitwise 56/167 — an accurate done/remaining ledger across the surface.
Tracks aggregate score to two decimals (99.88%→99.95%→99.96%), maps every remaining failure to specific files (14 conversions, 2 rounding, 1 call_indirect), quantifying the concrete gap to 1.0.
Detects that the unsigned-trunc fix caused regressions and decides to revert — catches a cross-family regression from its own change.

Identifies it is stuck on the rounding -0.0 case ('handler exists but never called'), distinguishing a stuck assertion from progress; however repeated Submit attempts (275,278,279) while unresolved show mild end-stretch churn.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent exhibits near-textbook top-anchor behavior: it maintains a precise done/remaining/blocked ledger over hundreds of opcodes, continuously reconciles per-family pass counts against the aggregate score, quantifies the gap to 1.0 concretely, ranks remaining work by highest-remaining-assertion buckets, and catches both a cross-family regression (step 273) and a stuck assertion (rounding -0.0). It falls just short of a perfect 10 because in the final stretch it repeatedly submitted while cycling on the last 17 failures without fully closing them out. This places it at 9.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions

evidence.note: Recognized the whole decode_simd opcode mapping was structurally wrong (hardcoded mapping conflicted with wasm-objdump), verified against ground truth, extracted 236 real opcodes and rewrote the shared decoder once — a root-cause refactor that flipped many SIMD families together (8-level behavior).

Diagnosed 'unexpected br(n) at top level' as a Br(n)-not-decremented root cause and fixed it at the block/loop boundary, taking block/return families to 100% — fixing the generator rather than instances.
Lane load/store operand order was reverted then re-fixed repeatedly, reasoning back and forth about pop order — clear circular re-debugging rather than a single decisive determination.
pmin/pmax semantics oscillated (a.min(b) vs wasm_min) and conversion trap-type change caused a regression to 95.43% then was reverted — surface guessing that broke green families temporarily.

Late-stage conversion trap-type and rounding/-0.0 fixes were tried, reverted, and retried multiple times without isolating the true cause, plateauing at 99.88% — persistent instance-by-instance patching on the last families.

dimensions.reasoning: The agent demonstrably recognized at least two structural divergences (the systematically wrong SIMD opcode mapping and the Br(n) propagation bug) and reworked the shared cause once so many downstream assertions flipped together — squarely the level-8 pattern. However, it does NOT cleanly avoid circular re-debugging: lane operand order, pmin/pmax semantics, and conversion trap types were reverted and re-applied repeatedly, at one point regressing the score. This mix of genuine root-cause refactoring plus notable oscillation places it between the 5 and 8 anchors, closer to 8, at a 7.

rubric.task_read: A long-horizon systems task: understand an existing partial Rust WASM interpreter, fix its bugs/unimplemented MVP functions, then add the entire 128-bit SIMD proposal — hundreds of opcodes across ~15 semantic families (memory, splat, lane, bitwise, int/float arith, saturating, widen/narrow, conversions, dot, q15). Difficulty comes from breadth (must not lose track), subtle exact semantics (saturation, NaN, rounding, lane order), a hard fixed-interface constraint, and an all-or-nothing 1.0 target measured by a provided per-assertion spec-test harness. A skilled practitioner invests heavily in orientation, family-level decomposition, and tight incremental verification.

dimensions.name: Interpreter & SIMD-encoding orientation
dimensions.description: Understanding the provided skeleton (Value model, decode/runtime/types, which functions are stubbed or buggy, the fixed public contract) and the SIMD binary encoding + lane semantics before and while implementing.
dimensions.why_it_matters: The task forbids rewriting and forbids touching spec.rs/main.rs or renaming public items; wrong assumptions about the existing Value representation or the 0xFD encoding propagate into every one of hundreds of opcodes. Getting exact per-family semantics (lane order, sat, NaN) is a research act, not guesswork.

anchors.0: Starts editing/adding opcodes without reading the existing sources or the spec-test format; invents an interface.
anchors.3: Skims one or two files; knows it's a WASM interpreter but not which functions are stubbed vs buggy, nor how v128 must slot into the existing Value type.
anchors.5: Reads decode.rs/runtime.rs/types.rs and identifies the public items that must not change, the existing value/stack model, and roughly how the 0xFD prefix + LEB sub-opcode is decoded; consults spec semantics for the common families.
anchors.8: Builds an explicit map of the codebase: what compiles, which MVP functions are unimplemented/buggy, exactly where value types, decoding, memory, and execution are wired, and how v128 must integrate without breaking the frozen interface. Pins down non-obvious semantics (saturation, NaN propagation, signed/unsigned lanes, extend low/high ordering) from the spec rather than guessing.
anchors.10: All of the above plus sustained, targeted re-research when a family behaves unexpectedly: probes specific spec-test cases to disambiguate encoding/rounding/lane-order questions, verifies the fixed public API surface concretely, and confirms encoding assumptions against wabt-generated output — orientation continually deepens as unfamiliar families are reached.

dimensions.name: Family-level decomposition & milestones
dimensions.description: Breaking the work into an ordered hierarchy — first MVP correctness, then SIMD by instruction family — each milestone tied to a concrete spec-test json as its done-check.
dimensions.why_it_matters: There are hundreds of opcodes but a clean natural structure (MVP first; then per-family, each with its own spec_json file). Treating it as one undifferentiated push guarantees losing the plot and thrashing across unrelated failures.

anchors.0: No structure; jumps between random opcodes with no ordering or notion of completion.
anchors.3: Vague two-phase idea ('do MVP then SIMD') with no sub-structure and no per-family done criteria.
anchors.5: Sequences MVP before SIMD and groups SIMD into a handful of families, implementing family by family with the matching spec test as a rough checkpoint.
anchors.8: Maintains an explicit ordered plan over the ~15 families with sensible dependency ordering (e.g. v128 value type + const/load/store and lane infra before arithmetic that depends on them), each milestone bound to a specific spec_json and a pass target, adjusted as families reveal shared infrastructure.
anchors.10: A living, dependency-aware milestone hierarchy: shared primitives (lane read/write, splat, per-shape iteration helpers) are sequenced first to avoid rework, families ordered by leverage, each with an explicit exit check, and the structure is revised as reality shifts scope — never a flat undifferentiated list, never redundant re-implementation across families.

dimensions.name: Incremental per-family verification
dimensions.description: Deliberately using the provided spec-test harness at fine granularity — per-family json files and the aggregate runner — to localize failures and confirm correctness rather than assuming it.
dimensions.why_it_matters: A 1.0 (all-assertions) target is unforgiving; the harness reports per-assertion pass/fail per file, so a strategy of running individual family jsons and reading FAIL lines is the difference between fast localization and blind flailing across a giant surface.

anchors.0: Never builds/runs the tests, or only at the very end; declares done without evidence.
anchors.3: Runs the full suite occasionally and reads only the final pass rate, without isolating which assertions fail or why.
anchors.5: Builds and runs the relevant per-family spec-test json after implementing each family, and uses FAIL lines to fix that family before moving on.
anchors.8: Systematic loop: implement family → run its json → read specific FAIL @ line reasons → fix → re-run to green, and periodically runs the full runner to confirm no regressions, keeping MVP files passing while adding SIMD.
anchors.10: Verification is engineered: drills into individual failing assertions to diagnose semantic edge cases (NaN, saturation boundaries, sign, lane order), distinguishes genuine bugs from encoding mismatches, guards against MVP regressions on every integration, and treats the aggregate score as a monitored signal rather than a one-shot final check — pursuing the exact 1.0 rather than 'mostly passing'.

dimensions.name: Coverage tracking across the opcode surface
dimensions.description: Maintaining an accurate picture of which families/opcodes are done, which remain, and which are stuck, across a very long implementation horizon.
dimensions.why_it_matters: With hundreds of opcodes and a strict 1.0 bar, an agent that loses track will either declare victory with families unimplemented or re-debug the same failing case in circles.

anchors.0: No sense of what's done vs remaining; forgets whole families or repeats work.
anchors.3: Rough mental sense of progress; frequently surprised by unimplemented opcodes or unnoticed regressions.
anchors.5: Keeps a checklist of families and current pass counts, updating it as families complete, and generally knows what remains.
anchors.8: Continuously reconciles per-family pass counts and the aggregate score against the full opcode list, notices when a fix in one family breaks another, and detects when it is stuck on a single assertion rather than making progress.
anchors.10: Maintains a precise done/remaining/blocked ledger over the whole surface, catches thrashing early (same FAIL recurring), quantifies the remaining gap to 1.0 concretely, and reallocates effort toward the highest-remaining-assertion families instead of polishing already-green ones — the plot is never lost across the long horizon.

dimensions.name: Course-correction on falsified assumptions
dimensions.description: Revising design or approach when reality diverges — e.g. a Value-type representation, decoding assumption, or semantic reading turns out wrong — rather than barrelling ahead.
dimensions.why_it_matters: Early choices (how v128 is stored, how lanes are read, how memory ops share code) and semantic guesses (sat/NaN/lane order) are easy to get subtly wrong; the fixed-interface constraint can also force a rethink. Detecting and reworking these beats piling fixes on a broken foundation.

anchors.0: Keeps applying local patches to a broken assumption; never revisits the root cause even as failures persist.
anchors.3: Occasionally tweaks approach under pressure but mostly forces the original plan regardless of evidence.
anchors.5: When a family stubbornly fails, steps back and reconsiders the relevant assumption (encoding, representation, or semantics) and adjusts.
anchors.8: Recognizes when a failure signals a structural problem (e.g. shared lane/decoding helper is wrong, or a value-representation choice can't satisfy the frozen interface) and refactors the shared cause once, so many downstream assertions flip together.
anchors.10: Proactively distinguishes root-cause divergence from surface bugs, reworks the foundation decisively and cleanly without breaking green families, and updates its plan/milestones to reflect the new understanding — demonstrably avoiding circular re-debugging by fixing the generator of failures rather than each instance.
